title: WPA work and buying a metal clarinet
summary: George worked WPA by day and played nights for a dollar, and bought a metal Albert-system clarinet.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: That was all in the 30s then? That was in the 30s.

Who played with you? Then besides that I waited. I was waking there for a dollar a night and Jeanette had been operating on it and I was waiting on the WPA. I'd catch the bus, the truck at 6 o'clock in the morning. I'd get off at 2 in the evening. I'd come in and work from 8.30 to 3 every night. Never miss a night and that's where I got that metal clarinet as well. Oh yeah? I'd buy that metal clarinet.
Where did you get that? You don't have it anymore do you? Yes, I got it. You still got it? I always like that. I got it. I got it. That would be fixed up. I got it. It sounded good, didn't it?
Yeah, I don't know if you get rid of that clarinet.
Well where's he got it though now?
From the Wuerlein. Mr. Voorhees used to work by Wuerlein. They had it there on the exhibition. He used to run that. So it was like a company, $40 something. $40 something actually.
Because I used to see them, I used to see the BAME systems in New York in 1930 were $10 metal metal.
Well this was a brand new home.
I mean you could get them new. Public schools all used in metal, $10. So the Alberts, I didn't know they made them in Alberts as much, but yours is Alberts. One piece was it?
One piece, yeah. The bell comes off and the mouth piece, that's all.
